audit.why: 50.57% over 1766 games with a TRICKY 7.5/10 and an 8.5/10 carry threat is a fair read of a lane you can hold but never safely close.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers render three different answers to who wins a phase. The full layer reads Tryndamere / Skill / Sion / Sion / Tryndamere / Sion / Sion; the content layer reads Tryndamere / Skill / Sion / Skill / Skill / Sion / Skill. Levels 4-5, Level 6 and 2+ items disagree.
audit.why: The packet chart matches the content layer exactly, and the content whys argue for it too — whys[3] describes Spinning Slash breaking your charge (contested, not yours), whys[4] says neither ultimate is a clean answer, whys[6] says you stay even by respecting his gap-close. The full layer is the one that is wrong on all three rows.
audit.corrected: Proposed the three full-layer sides as one atomic group so they land together and match the content values already on disk. phases[4].rating raised from 3/10 to 6/10 to match this file's convention for a Skill row (phases[1] is Skill at 6/10).

audit.whatIsWrong: Mocking Shout does not appear anywhere on the page, and the healing is attributed to his passive.
audit.why: Mocking Shout reduces surrounding champions' attack damage and slows enemies whose backs are turned to him — against a Sion with no dash, that means the moment you decide to leave a trade you are slowed for free, on a 14-second cooldown at 850 range. And Battle Fury only builds Fury and crit chance; Bloodlust is the ability that consumes Fury to heal, which is what anti-heal actually targets.
audit.corrected: Wrote Mocking Shout into mid, late and wants.foe[1], and corrected the heal to Bloodlust in whys[5] and late.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tryndamere.json P, Q and W text

audit.whatIsWrong: Undying Rage's cooldown is given as 110 seconds in whys[4] and again in mid.
audit.why: It is 120/100/80. The 110 figure is right at no rank, and the whole page is built on tracking that one number — 'if it has been more than 90 seconds since he last used it, do not start a committed brawl' is advice calibrated to a cooldown that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Corrected to 120 at rank 1 and 80 at rank 3 in both places, and added Spinning Slash's 12s rank-1 cooldown to mid.

edits.before: Both ultimates create all-in uncertainty — your R is a chase and engage tool but his R keeps him alive through your follow-ups. Track the 110-second R cooldown before every commit.
edits.after: Both ultimates create all-in uncertainty — your R chases and engages, his keeps him alive through your follow-up. Undying Rage is 120 seconds at rank 1 and still 80 at rank 3, so count it.

edits.before: Heartsteel HP and a large W-shield let you absorb a full crit burst and brawl back — buy anti-heal first to gut his fury passive regeneration during trades.
edits.after: Heartsteel and a large shield let you absorb a full crit burst and brawl back — buy anti-heal first: the healing is Bloodlust spending his Fury, not the passive.

edits.before: Spin-kite backward with his E to bait a telegraphed charged Q then re-engage after the whiff

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are the flattest stretch — your Q charge is readable and he can E-spin out of the telegraph while his fury-loaded crits keep ticking. Trade only when he has low fury and his E is on cooldown; otherwise hold your W and let the wave do the work. At level 6 neither ult is a clean win button: your Unstoppable Onslaught can chase him down or escape a bad spot, but his Undying Rage fully answers a full-pattern kill attempt the moment he dips low. Track the R cooldown at 110 seconds — if it has been more than 90 seconds since he last used it, do not start a committed brawl.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are the flattest stretch — your Q charge is readable and he can E-spin out of the telegraph. Trade only when his fury is low and Spinning Slash is down, 12 seconds at rank 1. Mocking Shout also slows anyone with their back turned, so the moment you turn to walk away he chases for free — disengage facing him. At level 6 neither ult is a clean win button: yours chases or escapes, his answers a kill attempt the moment he dips low. Undying Rage is 120 seconds at rank 1, so if you have not seen it spent, do not start a committed brawl.

edits.before: Heartsteel makes your W-shield substantial enough to eat an entire crit rotation, and your zombie passive means even a bad fight costs him time and HP. The lane stays roughly even because Tryndamere scales into a split-push monster too — his E gap-close and crit DPS 1v1 him will always be dangerous if you try to fight him without the W up. Anti-heal is mandatory: his passive fury restores a meaningful chunk of HP across a trade, which negates small leads. The win pattern late is simple: W-shield absorbs his opening spin burst, E-shreds his armor, charged Q lands the knockup, and you finish after Undying Rage expires — never before.
edits.after: Heartsteel makes your shield substantial enough to eat an entire crit rotation, and your zombie passive means even a bad fight costs him time and HP. The lane stays roughly even because Tryndamere scales into a split-push monster too — his gap-close and crit DPS make him dangerous any time you fight without W up. Anti-heal is mandatory, and aim it at the right ability: Bloodlust is the heal, spending the Fury his passive builds. The win pattern is simple: shield the opening burst, E-shred the armour, land the charged Q, finish after Undying Rage expires — never before, and never with your back turned into Mocking Shout.

notes: This matchup carried a live two-layer level-chart disagreement on three rows — Levels 4-5, Level 6 and 2+ items — exactly the failure the working rules describe, where the page shows a paying user two different answers to who wins a phase. The content layer and the packet agreed, so I moved the full layer onto them rather than the reverse. suspectNames flagged wants.foe[2] 'Pop Undying Rage' as a probable wrong name: false positive, that is his real R. No mirror audit exists for tryndamere vs sion yet, so the Mocking Shout and Bloodlust framing here is the first pass on this pair and should be reused rather than re-derived. The full layer contains the usual mojibake, so beyond the four enum tokens above I left it alone — note that report[0].t, tldr and dosFull[1].t all still say 'anti-heal his crits', which points at the wrong ability the same way whys[5] did.
